sampling_model.design: Abstract triangular rectangular fixed-design panel with \(N/T\to c\in(0,\infty)\) and one deterministic treated-post block.
sampling_model.units: The arrays \(d,qvec,a,b,\Lambda,F\) are fixed members of the exact-oracle class defined by the four stated orthogonality restrictions; those restrictions remove baseline-factor cross terms but do not select a profile minimizer. Randomness comes only from iid Gaussian \(E_{it}\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(D=dqvec^{\top}\), with heterogeneous treated-post component \(\theta(d\odot a)(qvec\odot b)^{\top}/\sqrt m\).
sampling_model.overlap: The scalar shares \(p_N\) and \(q_T\) have interior limits \(p\) and \(q\). The restricted Grams use the diagonal control selector \(M_d\) and diagonal pre-period selector \(M_{qvec}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Full-sample IFE profiles rank \(r+1\) with smallest-coefficient, lexicographic best-approximation, and lexicographic subspace-completion rules. The internal masked benchmark fits rank \(r\) only on \(D_{it}=0\), with radii containing the normalized true baseline. Both intervals use their stated residual degrees of freedom and nonnegative-root conventions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The profiled IFE coefficient is consistent and asymptotically normal under strong-factor and identification conditions.
The slope limit distribution is invariant to fitting more factors than the true rank under the paper's regularity conditions.
A fixed rectangular finite-rank perturbation separates from the noise edge exactly above the \(D\)-transform threshold.
Bias-aware intervals attain uniform coverage over factor strength under generalized regressor non-collinearity.
With an asymptotically strong treatment-effect factor, full-sample IFE converges to the common component \(\gamma\) rather than ATT.
Tall-wide factor imputation yields pointwise asymptotic normality for an ATT estimator under strong observed-block factor conditions.
IFE with a growing fitted factor count converges to a conditional-variance-weighted average of heterogeneous treatment effects.
Potential-factor models identify systematic causal effects and provide feasible counterfactual inference using untreated or treatment-specific factor structure.

body.tldr: This paper studies an abstract exact-oracle panel limit experiment in which four finite-array orthogonality restrictions remove ordinary baseline-confounding terms without determining the profiled coefficient. Whole-sample IFE can then absorb a bounded local heterogeneous treatment effect when its rectangular spike becomes detectable. The paper derives the coefficient-indexed two-by-two profile, proves the absorption law on compact stable-singleton geometries, maps an absorbed region into conventional-Wald undercoverage, and uses masked fitting only as an internal benchmark control. The large-signal endpoint is solely a deterministic profile calculation, and selection at genuine ties remains open.

project_justification.gap: Existing panel theory covers regular strong factors, generic weak-factor robustness, or the strong bad-control endpoint, while random-matrix theory fixes the spike before taking limits. None controls a bounded coefficient-indexed treatment spike in the global IFE criterion after ordinary baseline-confounding terms have been removed by defining restrictions.
project_justification.niche: An exact-oracle noise-scale treatment factor creates a nonregular sensitivity experiment connecting harmless over-fitting to ATT absorption.
project_justification.fill: The project derives \(\Phi_{\eta,h}\), proves bounded-local profile convergence and the absorption map on stable-singleton geometries, isolates tie selection as an open question, derives conventional-Wald failure, and uses masked fitting only as an internal control within the same abstract experiment.

body.related_work: Bai (2009) supplies the moment and limiting Gram framework for regular profiled IFE; the deterministic Gram envelopes, maximum-row bounds, and treatment-score bounds here are this paper's own sufficient regularity conditions. Moon and Weidner (2015) show harmless rank overestimation under a class excluding low-rank regressors. Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2012) supply fixed-spike rectangular outlier maps, while Bloemendal and Virag (2013) describe near-critical edge laws. Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) inform the weak-factor inference question but exclude the rank-one block treatment through non-collinearity. Cardoso, Ferman, and Fernandes (2026) establish the strong treatment-factor bad-control endpoint, not the bounded local path. Juodis and Weidner (2026) characterize variance-weighted limits under growing fitted rank. Bai and Ng (2021) inform tall-wide imputation, restricted observed-block Gram conditions, and pointwise ATT theory; masked fitting here is only an internal control using the actual diagonal control and pre-period selectors and explicit normalization, radius, and residual-degrees-of-freedom conventions. Bai and Wang (2026) organize causal effects through potential factor structures rather than a whole-sample absorption profile. Gobillon and Magnac (2016) motivate studying whole-sample and counterfactual factor fits; the exact-oracle theorem has no direct operational implication for their empirical setting.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The four exact orthogonality restrictions define the admissible triangular-array class. They remove baseline-factor cross terms so that coefficient distortion isolates absorption by the fitted singular direction, but they do not select a minimizer of the profile. Masking is not itself the novelty and says nothing about ordinary baseline-confounding bias outside this class. If separated minima admit opposite \(m^{-1/4}\) nuisance drifts with identical limiting coordinates but different selections, no selector indexed only by \((\eta,h)\) is valid. The stochastic theorems therefore stop at bounded stable-singleton geometries.
body.honest_scope: The proposal is an abstract exact-oracle sensitivity benchmark. The stochastic profile, selection, absorption, and Wald claims concern only \(\theta\in[-K,K]\), \(h\in[-\overline h,\overline h]\), and compact stable-singleton geometries. The limit \(|h|\to\infty\) belongs solely to a deterministic profile proposition. Complete global minimizer classification and drift-sensitive tie selection remain open. Exact finite-array orthogonality is a defining restriction, not an observable residualization procedure, and it does not encode which profile minimizer is selected. Masked fitting is only an internal control; neither it nor the oracle class is claimed as a new practical estimator. At \(\theta=0\), the profile reduces to the homogeneous-effect benchmark.
